# DoNext city research — 17 September 2026

`checkedAt: 2026-09-17T08:16:00+01:00`

Review window: Thursday 17–Friday 18 September and the weekend of Saturday 19–Sunday 20 September 2026. Primary organiser and venue pages were opened afresh. The live city catalogs still carry a 12 September update stamp and were treated as stale context, not as fresh verification.

## Bristol — eight credible candidates

1. **Aardman mini-museum hunt — selected for today's campaign.** Bristol Museum & Art Gallery, free detective map and tiny Aardman treasures hidden around the museum; families and curious explorers of all ages; runs until 1 November. Museum entry is free and opening hours are Tuesday–Sunday 10am–5pm. The British and World Wildlife Galleries are currently closed. Sources: https://www.bristolmuseums.org.uk/whats-on/bristol-museum-and-art-gallery/mini-museum-hunt-aardman/ and https://www.bristolmuseums.org.uk/bristol-museum-and-art-gallery/plan-your-visit/opening-times/
2. **Bristol Sea Shanty Shout.** Great Eastern Hall, Brunel Square, Saturday 19 and Sunday 20 September, noon–6pm. Free, no booking; donations accepted. Twelve shanty crews across the two days; this free programme is not on the ship. https://www.bristoldockyards.org/whats-on/bristol-sea-shanty-shout
3. **Trinity Community Celebration Day.** Sunday 20 September, noon–4pm; £0–£3 donation; all ages, under-14s with an adult. Music, youth performances, all-age workshops, nature and craft drop-ins. Accessibility requests by email. https://www.trinitybristol.org.uk/whats-on/2026/trinitys-community-day-celebration
4. **Docks Heritage Weekend.** M Shed, Saturday 19–Sunday 20 September. Free museum programme includes a docks quiz trail through Sunday, quayside theatre, cargo demonstrations and models; Saturday includes paper-boat making and colouring. Crane visits and boat trips are charged. Exact family-workshop times are not published, so do not promise a slot. https://www.bristolmuseums.org.uk/whats-on/m-shed/docks-heritage-weekend/
5. **Tyntesfield Heritage Open Days.** Free entry through Sunday 20 September, 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm; no booking; everyone welcome. Sloping paths and loose gravel; mobility shuttle 10am–5pm. https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/tyntesfield/events/181b773f-1fc7-4a87-8f4b-41c89c2dd4c8
6. **Dyrham Park Heritage Open Days.** Free entry and parking Thursday 17–Saturday 19 September, 10am–5pm, last entry 4pm; no booking; all ages. This was already included in the 14 September estates campaign, so do not create another standalone post. https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/dyrham-park/events/94f2b171-9191-4b0e-a234-810e59b3fe3f
7. **Arnold Art Cart.** Free self-led family making at Arnolfini, Tuesday–Sunday 11am–6pm. Already promoted and confirmed published on 15 September; retain as an indoor backup but do not repeat it. https://arnolfini.org.uk/whatson/arnold-art-cart/
8. **Central Library rhyme and story time.** Free all-year library timetable for ages 0–3 with older siblings welcome; around 20 minutes, no booking. Already promoted and confirmed published on 16 September; retain as a weekday source but do not repeat it this week. https://www.bristol.gov.uk/residents/libraries-and-archives/services-for-children-and-young-people/baby-bounce-and-rhyme-and-storytime-sessions

The selected hunt gives a distinct indoor, all-age option and avoids recycling the three most recent Bristol campaigns.

## Cardiff — current shortlist

1. **St Margaret's Open Doors:** Saturday 19 September 12:30–5:30pm and Sunday 20 September 2–5:30pm; free, no booking; children's quiz trail. Tower ascent is able-bodied adults only; disabled church entry is through the porch. https://cadw.gov.wales/open-doors-st-margarets-church-roath
2. **Penylan LEGO Club:** weekly Saturday 10–11am; free drop-in; ages 2+. The recurring page does not explicitly date 19 September, so advise confirming before a special journey. https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/hub-events/clwb-lego/
3. **National Museum Cardiff:** free general admission Saturday and Sunday 10am–5pm, galleries close 4:45pm; under-16s with an adult. Advance free day ticket is optional wording rather than a condition of entry; parking is £6.50. https://museum.wales/cardiff/visit/
4. **Bute Park sculpture hunt:** more than twenty wooden sculptures, including climbable frog, beetle and hollow log pieces; current park hours 7:30am–6:45pm. Free self-led ordinary park visit. https://bute-park.com/attraction/sculpture-trail/
5. **Insole Court garden tour:** Sunday 20 September, sessions hourly 10am–3pm; free/donations, about 45 minutes on uneven paths; advance tickets only and no walk-ups. The organiser page does not specify child suitability or current ticket availability, so keep as an adult-led optional extra rather than a headline family pick. https://cadw.gov.wales/open-doors-insole-court
6. **Rhydypennau story and rhyme:** Friday 10:30–11:15am; free, no booking; under-5s. Weekday subscriber option. https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/hub-events/story-and-rhyme-time-english/

## Birmingham — current shortlist

1. **Brum Transport Fest:** Friday 18 and Saturday 19 September, 11am–5pm; free, no booking; classic vehicles, buses, museum exhibits, family activities and live stage. Outdoor and wheelchair accessible. Chamberlain Square remains marked TBC. https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/brum-transport-festival/
2. **Moor Pool Heritage Festival:** Sunday 20 September, 11am–3pm; free, no booking; crafts, trails, LEGO, sport tasters and brass band. Some estate routes have steps or uneven surfaces; side wheelchair entrance to the hall. https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/moor-pool-heritage-festival/
3. **Make a Mini Museum:** Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery, Sunday 20 September, 11am–3pm; free drop-in; all ages with adult supervision. https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/events/marvellous-makers
4. **Explore Blakesley:** Saturday 19 September, grounds 11am–4pm and timed Hall entry 11am–3pm; £5 adult/£3 child; all ages; pre-book essential. https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/events/heritage-open-day-and-birmingham-heritage-week-explore-blakesley
5. **Lapworth Museum:** fossils, minerals and Roary the Jurassic predator; free, no booking; September weekend hours noon–5pm; pram/wheelchair access and baby change. https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/cultural-attractions/lapworth-museum-of-geology/visit-us
6. **Helios:** illuminated Sun sculpture at The Exchange; free, no booking; Saturday 8am–5pm and closed Sunday. https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/the-exchange/events/helios
